title: Create work order raises one estimate WO per row
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor (view customers; edit customers to raise a work order), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. Open Customers from the top navigation and switch to its "Maintenance reminders" tab. For the location cases use a two-workplace org (on a one-workplace org the location filter is absent).
  3. A row whose service schedule belongs to the header location, and a unit on two schedules with services falling close together.
custom_steps:
1. On a row use Create work order and read the new work order's status, customer/asset, and whether the service's canned lines are added.
  2. Confirm it opens the work order and the row's Work Order column then links to it.
  3. Note the workplace the work order is raised at.
  4. On the two-schedule unit, confirm each row has its own Create work order.
  5. Look for any way to raise one work order covering several assets.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Create work order creates a work order in estimate status for that customer and asset; where the service's schedule belongs to the header location it adds the service's canned lines and opens the work order, and the row's Work Order column links to it; it is raised at the header location.
  • A work order is created per row - there is no multi-asset work order.
  • A unit on two schedules whose services fall close together produces two rows, each with its own Create work order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10570 (S13, The worklist); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S13; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

The row's Work Order column then links to it per S13-R14”
  • S13-R38: “Create work order raises the work order at the location chosen in the header, as creating a work order does today”
  • S13-E1: “A unit on two schedules whose services fall close together produces two rows, each with its own Create work order”
